newsitem.title: USA: New York airport ring allegedly stole, took bribes.
newsitem.headline: New York airport ring allegedly stole, took bribes.

text.p: Seven former employees of an American Airlines subsidiary at La Guardia Airport were accused on Tuesday of taking bribes and stealing money from suspected drug traffickers, authorities said.

The seven, including security personnel, skycaps and a baggage handler, were employed by AMR Services, a subsidiary of American Airlines, at screening checkpoints for American flights, U.S. Attorney Zachary Carter said.
They allegedly developed a system of identifying drug traffickers likely to be carrying large amounts of cash, the federal prosecutor said.

When airport X-ray machines confirmed their suspicions, they would pull the suspect aside and demand bribes, Carter said. In other cases, they simply stole currency from passengers' checked luggage, he said.
The prosecutor estimated they stole or accepted bribes totaling hundreds of thousands of dollars and let millions of dollars' worth of narcotics pass through the airport.
Their scheme unraveled when two Colombian travelers complained to authorities that La Guardia security employees stole $280,000 from them early in May, Carter said.
The accused, none of whom now work for AMR, comprised two security supervisors, two skycap captains, a security checkpoint agent, a baggage handler and a general manager.
